history.period: Ancient - believed 2000-3000 years old; referenced in Sangam literature and the Silapathikaram
history.summary: The second of the Arupadai Veedu (six abodes of Murugan) and the only one at sea level, standing on the shores of the Gulf of Mannar (puranic name Jayanthipuram). The temple marks the spot where Murugan is said to have worshipped his father Shiva after defeating the demon Surapadma. Its nine-storey rajagopuram (~157 ft) unusually faces west because the sea lies to the east; notable features include the Nazhi Kinaru well and shrines built of black granite. In the 17th century the Dutch occupied the temple and looted idols, which legend says were thrown into the sea and later recovered after Murugan revealed their location to a devotee; the British later shored up the sea-eroded foundations. It was the fourth Hindu temple in Tamil Nadu to receive ISO certification. name: Tiruchendur Murugan Temple (Senthil Andavar Temple)
town_description: Coastal town in Thoothukudi district on the Gulf of Mannar; pilgrim town known for the seashore Subramanya Swamy temple, the only Arupadai Veedu at sea level.

travel.airport: Tuticorin (Thoothukudi) Airport (~55 km); Madurai International Airport (~140 km)
travel.road: Buses from Tirunelveli (~40 km), Thoothukudi (~38 km), Madurai, Kanyakumari (~90 km) and Chennai (~630 km)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Kanda Sashti (Oct-Nov) draws the largest crowds
